correctness.rationale: The legal de Bruijn overlap digraph is strongly connected (append a nonzero character then construct any target). At k>h, indegree/outdegree defects arise precisely at vertices beginning/ending with 0^(h-1), with the overlap correction at k=2h. Source set S and sink set T each have M vertices. For d=k-h, every S-to-T directed path must have length >=d because a shorter arrival in 0^(h-1) would force forbidden 0^h from overlapping marked zero runs; appending the final d symbols of each T yields a unique legal bridge. Any additional balanced edge flow in a covering cycle decomposes into >=M S→T paths and nonnegative circuits, giving lower bound d*M; adding chosen M shortest bridges yields an Eulerian multigraph. Independent legal graph assembly, BFS every defect source→sink and extra cost matched in 8 cases q=2,3 h=2,3; binary q=2,h=3 gives 14,28,53 and ternary q=3,h=3,k=6 gives 696.

final_claim: For labeled q>=2, h>=2 and h<=k<=2h, shortest cyclic cover of every legal length-k factor avoiding 0^h has L=A_(q,h)(k)+(k-h)*M, where M(h)=0 and M(k)=(q-1)*(q^(k-h-1)-1_(k=2h)). Every optimal extra-flow path matches a defect source to sink via its unique k-h edge bridge; any bijection yields an Eulerian optimal cover.
